Customer needs EU data residency for EU customers, strict log retention rules (no persistent PII in logs), SOC2/ISO evidence, KMS-based key management, and clarity on what Redwood stores/keeps. SE will follow up with architecture for private VPC/on-prem and PoC scope for benchmarking latency/cost.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Rodriguez (CISO - Westfield), Alan Kim (Dir, Cloud Arch), Priya Singh (Compliance)

[00:00] Laura Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're excited to learn about Westfield's requirements around data residency and compliance. quick round of intros?
[00:08] Maya Rodriguez: Maya here, CISO at Westfield, and, yeah, main interest is making sure any LLM usage meets our regulatory controls, especially for EU customers.
[00:15] Alan Kim: Alan, director of cloud arch, i'll be focused on network, VPC, egress rules, and how the deployment fits our infra.
[00:21] Priya Singh: Priya, compliance — looking for clarity on logging, retention, and whether we can prevent PII from being written to any vendor logs.
[00:28] Laura Chen: Great. Samir is our solutions engineer, he'll answer the nitty gritty on private deployments and what we persist. Samir?
[00:34] Samir Patel: Hi all. Quick agenda — goals, current stack, residency needs, logging/retention, encryption/KMS questions, and then next steps/PoC.

[02:15] Laura Chen: To start, can you walk us through your current stack and how you plan to call models? is it direct app traffic, or via a backend — typical?
[02:28] Alan Kim: We proxy everything through our internal API gateway. For US customers we run in us-east, for EU customers we have eu-west region. We want model hosting to be able to guarantee data doesn't leave EU for EU customers — so geo-fencing or private deployment is interesting.
[02:42] Priya Singh: Also need to understand if complete request/response payloads are logged by the vendor, even if redacted. Our policy forbids persistent logs with raw customer PII.

[04:05] Samir Patel: On Redwood hosted — our hosted API runs in multiple regions, we offer region pinning where feasible but we do operate multi-region control planes. For strict residency we usually recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private — Dedicated gives you reserved capacity in a region and stronger isolation; Private gives you customer-managed control plane and can be VPC or on-prem.
[04:32] Maya Rodriguez: When you say "control plane" multi-region — does that mean auth or metadata could cross borders? any personal data in those control-plane logs?
[04:40] Samir Patel: Good question. The control plane does maintain metadata for routing and billing; we have options: for Dedicated we can limit control-plane telemetry to region and for Private the control plane can be deployed in your VPC or on-prem so nothing leaves your network. we can also turn off non-essential analytics.

[06:12] Priya Singh: Do you have SOC 2 or ISO certifications? we need to present the vendor evidence.
[06:18] Laura Chen: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestation — i'll send the security pack and the reports after this call.
[06:26] Priya Singh: Great. Also, what about HIPAA — we have a small set of customers that are financial advisors with health benefit data, how is PHI handled?
[06:35] Samir Patel: We have HIPAA controls available for private deployments; on hosted we can sign BAAs for certain enterprise accounts but usually private deployments are recommended for strict PHI workloads because you control logs and key management.

[08:00] Alan Kim: On the dedicated offering, is the KV cache or any persistent token store shared across tenants? we need strict tenancy separation.
[08:09] Samir Patel: No, Dedicated gives you tenant-isolated pools — KV cache is per-tenant. For shared-hosted, we use per-tenant namespaces but some metadata may be more co-located for efficiency. For the bank, we usually propose Dedicated or Private to meet separation requirements.

[10:55] Maya Rodriguez: Can you describe what exactly you log from a request? request/response bodies, prompts, tokens?
[11:03] Samir Patel: By default we retain limited telemetry for billing and quality — minimal request metadata, token counts, latency metrics. Request and response bodies are not retained persistently for Dedicated by default; for hosted we retain them for a configurable short window unless you request redaction or disable logging. For Private, you control logs — Redwood can be configured to write only sanitized logs to your logging sink.
[11:30] Priya Singh: When you say "configurable short window" — are we talking hours, days? we require retention under 30 days for most logs and redaction of PII within 24 hours.
[11:40] Samir Patel: Typical hosted default is 30 days for request traces, but we can reduce to lower windows for enterprise contracts; for Dedicated we can commit to custom retention windows in the contract. For Private, retention is whatever your policy enforces since you host the logs.

[13:12] Laura Chen: On encryption — do you support customer-managed keys? HSM integration?
[13:18] Samir Patel: Yes — for Dedicated and Private you can bring-your-own-keys (BYOK) via KMS integrations; we support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM-backed flows for on-prem. Hosted customers can also have CMEK in certain tiers.

[15:05] Alan Kim: Network egress — for Private/VPC deployments can we lock egress to only internal endpoints? our security team needs no outbound to the public internet from inference nodes.
[15:12] Samir Patel: Absolutely. Private deployments are designed to be deployed inside your VPC with strict egress rules. We have an architecture doc with recommended security groups and NAT/proxy configs — i'll share that.

[18:40] Priya Singh: GDPR: we need assurance around data subject requests and how we can delete all associated logs for a subject. can you do per-customer or per-subject deletion?
[18:52] Samir Patel: For Private, yes — you control data lifecycle. For Dedicated we provide tooling for deletion and purging of customer data; for hosted we support deletions but there are caveats around backups and cross-region caches — we can commit to deletion SLAs in contract. We'll need to map exact data flows to provide definitive timelines.

[21:20] Maya Rodriguez: Are you able to provide an architecture where EU customer requests are served only within EU infrastructure and not egressing to US?
[21:29] Samir Patel: Yes, region pinning plus Dedicated pools in eu-west will ensure inference processing and cache stay in EU. For absolute guarantees, Private control plane in your EU VPC is the cleanest approach.

[24:00] Alan Kim: For latency-sensitive tasks, we care about model selection — if we pick a quantized open model, what's the latency delta between hosted and private deployments? we may need benchmarking.
[24:12] Samir Patel: Latency depends on hardware and network — Dedicated on the same cloud region typically matches hosted latency; Private on-prem will vary depending on local GPUs. We can run a PoC to benchmark tail latency with your prompt set.

[28:30] Priya Singh: Logging details again — we can't have raw prompts persisted. Can you do on-the-fly redaction, or do we need to do pre-processing?
[28:40] Samir Patel: You can do either: pre-process to strip PII or we can configure runtime redaction rules in the inference pipeline to scrub sensitive fields before logging. There's slight added latency for runtime redaction but it's usually small.

[31:15] Maya Rodriguez: And audit logs for admin actions — we need tamper-evident audit trails for model rollouts and key rotation.
[31:24] Laura Chen: We have audit logging for admin and deployment changes; for Dedicated we can forward logs to your SIEM and support WORM storage for audit trails.

[34:50] Alan Kim: For the PoC — what do you need from us? examples of traffic, prompt catalog, compliance checklists?
[34:57] Samir Patel: Ideally: a sample prompt set (sanitized), list of models to test, throughput/latency SLOs, and the retention/logging policy you want enforced. We'll propose a 2-week PoC: week 1 deploy in a Dedicated EU pool + run synthetic load; week 2 run customer prompts and measure.

[38:10] Priya Singh: Contract questions — is there an option to have a BAA for PHI, and can the contract specify specific retention and deletion SLAs?
[38:19] Laura Chen: Yes on both — enterprise contracts can include BAA and explicit retention/deletion SLAs. We'll loop in legal after this and share a redlineable contract example.

[41:00] Maya Rodriguez: Anything else on security posture? vulnerability scanning, pen testing?
[41:08] Samir Patel: We run regular pen tests and third-party vuln scans; results are in the security pack i'll send. We also offer a hardened on-prem appliance for customers that require air-gapped or HSM-only key management.

[45:30] Alan Kim: One last network question — for Dedicated, is there a way to do private peering vs public internet?
[45:36] Samir Patel: Yes, we support VPC peering/private interconnect for Dedicated deployments on major clouds. For Private on-prem we'll use direct connect or private connectivity according to your network team.

[48:00] Laura Chen: OK quick recap and next steps: i'll send SOC2/ISO pack and security docs; Samir will share the VPC and private deployment architecture doc + PoC proposal; Priya will confirm retention windows and any additional legal/regulatory checkboxes; we'll schedule the SE deep dive and PoC planning for the week of March 16th.
[48:20] Maya Rodriguez: sounds good. One ask — can you include a diagram showing where logs are stored and how key rotation works? that's often helpful for our auditors.
[48:30] Samir Patel: Yes i'll include a key rotation flow and logging sink diagram.

[50:45] Priya Singh: Thanks all — appreciate the clarity.
[50:49] Laura Chen: Thank you — we'll follow up with docs and propose times for the deep dive.
[50:55] Alan Kim: Thanks.
[50:56] Maya Rodriguez: Bye.

(Transcript ends early for brevity; full call audio captured, timestamps approximate.)
